jobs.title: Economic Mobility Partnerships Manager - Career Pathways
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic's Beneficial Deployments team exists to ensure AI's benefits reach the people and communities that markets typically leave behind. As our work in Economic Mobility builds momentum, we're hiring a partnerships manager dedicated to career pathways in the AI age. You'll lead Claude Corps, our $150M flagship early career program — a national fellowship placing 1,000 early-career fellows, paid full-time for a year, with nonprofits serving communities across the U.S. Designed and run with CodePath, you'll own the program's success through its first cohorts and its evolution into replicable workforce infrastructure for the field if the program is impactful for both fellows and nonprofit host organizations. Beyond Claude Corps, you'll grow our talent developer partnerships — building on momentum like our CodePath partnership that infuses Claude and Claude Code in courses that reach 20,000+ students at community colleges, universities and workforce programs across the country. You will also lead workforce-related deployments on AI Fluency and Claude fluency with national and regional partners, helping workers build the skills to shape their own pathways in the AI transition. This is program and partnership leadership with real stakes on a global scale. The economic mobility field is early in its AI journey, and the organizations we work with choose Anthropic because of values alignment. You'll earn and keep that trust by delivering measurable results by supporting millions of people and their pathways through our partners by 2027. The role rewards entrepreneurial orchestration: building new programs amid ambiguity, scaling what works, and enabling partners to manage mature programs so you can build what's next. Key responsibilities Lead Claude Corps end-to-end — cohort launches, host organization pipeline, coordination with CodePath, program measurement, and the open-source playbook Develop and close tier-1 partnerships with talent developers, workforce organizations, and philanthropic and public sector partners — from scoping and structuring through deployment, measurement, and scale Deploy AI Fluency workforce development offerings for states and cities, and drive adoption of AI Fluency and Claude fluency training with national and regional partners Orchestrate across functions — working with Anthropic Academy, Economic Research, Applied AI, Policy, Communications, and GTM teams inside Anthropic, and with funders and agencies outside it Understand what works through research and share through open, replicable models the broader workforce field can use You may be a good fit if you: Have personally structured and led large, multi-year, multi-stakeholder partnerships — corporate, nonprofit, or public sector — and can speak to outcomes you advanced, not just agreements you signed Have operated inside a large or fast-growing company — on a people, talent, or HR team, or as a sponsor of talent and early career programs Have real substance in AI fluency, technical training, or learning programs — you have built, deployed, or led training and talent development work, not just advised on it Build well amid ambiguity — you create structure where none exists, adapt quickly when programs shift, and prioritize execution for impact over process Communicate at an executive level — your writing is exec-ready, you are a confident public speaker, and you move fluidly between corporate, nonprofit, and government audiences Strong candidates may also have: Experience designing learning programs end-to-end An existing network across workforce development, philanthropy, or the public sector Hands-on fluency with Claude — workflows, tools, or assets you have personally built This is a full-time role based in our San Francisco headquarters. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. cold_email.body:
Dear Pfizer Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Associate, Cyber Resilience opportunity with Pfizer at Pfizer.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.description: Important: This position will work in one of the following three Extended-Hours Support (ExHS) shift teams: 1. Weekend Shift Team 1a. Rotation 1: Sunday to Thursday (9AM–5PM), Friday and Saturday off 1b. Rotation 2: Tuesday to Saturday (9AM–5PM), Sunday and Monday off 2. Early-Morning Shift Team 2a. Rotation 1: Monday to Friday (4AM–12PM Pacific Time), Saturday and Sunday off 2b. Rotation 2: Tuesday to Saturday (4AM–12PM Pacific Time), Sunday and Monday off 3. Late-Evening Shift Team 3a. Rotation 1: Monday to Friday (3PM–11PM Pacific Time), Saturday and Sunday off 3b. Rotation 2: Sunday to Thursday (3PM–11PM Pacific Time), Friday and Saturday off Important notes: During hiring, candidates will select and commit to one shift team (Weekend, Early-Morning, or Late-Evening). Once hired and onboarded, the team member will work exclusively within that shift team. ExHS team members rotate quarterly (every three months) between their team's two rotations. There are no rotations between shift teams. This is an exciting opportunity in our Data Science Production Engineering (DSPE) department at Natera (a global leader in precision medicine and genomics testing), to lead a team providing key data analytics services for our lab production operations. As a Manager of Data Analysis for Lab Production Support, you will work in one of the above three DSPE Extended-Hours Support (ExHS) shift teams, during the specified rotation hours. You will have the opportunity to apply innovative data analytics solutions, directly support the most cutting-edge medical diagnostics and genomics applications, and make real & immediate impact to patients and healthcare providers, by ensuring the specific ExHS shift team's timely and accurate data analytics support to production teams, e.g., product management team, lab operations teams, lab director teams, and genetic counselor teams. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: Leadership Lead and mentor the specific ExHS shift team, fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, and collaboration. Measure, report, and continuously improve team operational effectiveness. Define and track team objectives, ensuring alignment with broader organizational goals. Provide career growth opportunities, feedback, and performance assessments for team members. Encourage individual contributors (ICs) to pitch ideas for process improvements and innovations. Operational Excellence Ensure timely and accurate resolution of production escalations data analysis tickets. Train and coach team members on new technologies, procedures, and guidelines/best practices. Enforce operating procedures for compliance, quality, and efficiency. Manage and improve tracking systems for workload, capacity, and ticket SLAs. Communication and Collaboration Represent the Extended-Hours Support (ExHS) teams in stakeholder meetings. Proactively manage stakeholder expectations. Establish regular stakeholder reporting mechanisms. Translate complex analytical results into actionable recommendations for cross-functional partners. Effectively and correctly escalate issues encountered to other DSPE teams. Process Improvement and Innovation Identify opportunities for automation and process enhancements to streamline operations. Identify and escalate risks such as data model changes that impact project timelines or ticket TAT. Collaborate with the overall DSPE team to develop new and improve existing support solutions. QUALIFICATIONS: Master's degree in a related field (e.g., Statistics, Data Science, Computer Science). Minimum 5 years of working experience in a highly regulated environment, e.g., CLIA and/or FDA compliant settings. Minimum 5 years of hands-on experience in data analysis and/or statistical modeling in data production, data engineering, data analytics, analytics production support roles. Minimum 2 years in a team management role. Knowledge of regulatory requirements, such as HIPAA and FDA guidelines. Working knowledge of the business processes and requirements of diagnostic laboratories. Proven track record in managing production escalations, data workflows, and team operations. Experience with healthcare data, and clinical terminology is a plus. Functional understanding of next-gen sequencing workflows. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES: Proficient in data analysis and statistical techniques. Proficient in Python and SQL development. Working knowledge of Snowflake platform technologies. Strong SQL skills for querying and retrieving data from complex data sources in a structured format. Strong understanding of various statistical concepts (parametric & non-parametric distributions, hypothesis testing, probability, regression). Proficient in aggregating data, preparing, cleaning data, and data mining using SQL and Python. Familiarity with machine learning techniques and their practical applications in real-world datasets. Strong leadership and team management skills. Excellent problem-solving and critical-thinking abilities. Good documentation practices and coding style. Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present technical findings to both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience using version control systems such as GitHub or GitLab for managing code and collaboration. Attention to detail and a commitment to data accuracy. Ability to work collaboratively in a cross-functional team environment. Strong integrity. cold_email.subject: Interest in Manager of Data Analysis for Lab Production Support, Extended-Hours Support (ExHS) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Manager of Data Analysis for Lab Production Support, Extended-Hours Support (ExHS) opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Strategic Finance Analyst
jobs.description: About Datadog: Datadog is the essential monitoring and security platform for cloud applications. We bring together end-to-end traces, metrics, and logs to make your applications, infrastructure, and third-party services entirely observable. These capabilities help businesses secure their systems, avoid downtime, and ensure customers are getting the best user experience. The Team: Datadog's Finance team collaborates with teams across the organization, providing commercial, operational and analytical support to ensure that Datadog's business continues to scale rapidly and efficiently. The Opportunity: Strategic Finance partners with the business to analyze key financial and operational drivers across the company in order to support the business’ growth and success. As an analyst supporting revenue, you will manage and refine key financial models and data, help create our annual financial targets, and work directly with operational leaders across multiple functions to support execution against our goals. Your work will be highly cross-functional and play a pivotal role in connecting the dots across the organization through a financial lens, ensuring operational alignment and informing decision making. What You’ll Do: Manage financial forecasts and analyses that may include revenue, ARR, customers, product, and cash flow - translating insights into recommendations for senior leaders Partner with senior business leaders across various departments, such as go-to-market (GTM) and Product to track performance and assess trends Work with finance management on quarterly Board materials, including coordination and consolidation across stakeholders Partner with the Accounting team for monthly / quarterly flux analysis and financial close items Assist in planning and budgeting cycles, ensuring consistency in tools, templates, and processes across the organization Become proficient with various financial planning and business intelligence (BI) tools, including but not limited to Pigment, Tableau, and Metabase Assist with ROI and profitability analyses on regional and sales channel levels to support data-driven decision making Work on ad hoc projects and strategic initiatives for senior management, which may include assessing analyzing various business challenges / opportunities and proposing solutions Who You Are: 2+ years of professional experience in FP&A, Corporate Finance, Investment Banking, or other related field Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, business, or economics Mastery of Excel and PowerPoint with proven experience in building financial models and managing complex data You are a clear, concise communicator and team player with a humble mindset and ‘can-do’ attitude MBA or CFA is a plus but not required; Solid understanding of Pigment or other EPM software is a plus, but not required Experience in or understanding of a consumption-based software business model Benefits and Growth : Generous and competitive benefits package New hire stock equity (RSUs) and employee stock purchase plan Continuous career development and pathing opportunities Product training to develop an in-depth understanding of our product and space Friendly and inclusive workplace culture Work Location: At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them. This role will require you to work in the office 3 days per week, and flexible the remainder. #LI-Hybrid Datadog offers a competitive salary and equity package, and may include variable compensation. Actual compensation is based on factors such as the candidate's skills, qualifications, and experience. It brings applications, infrastructure, data, models, and security into one place, using AI to detect and resolve issues before they impact customers. Trusted globally by Fortune 500 companies and high-growth AI leaders, Datadog enables businesses to move faster with clarity and confidence. Learn more about #DatadogLife on Instagram , LinkedIn, and Datadog Learning Center. jobs.description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. Manager, PV Analytics Center of Excellence – JD The Manager, PV Analytics Center of Excellence is responsible for successful execution, and close-out of activities aligned with the overall vision, strategy, and objectives of the Patient Safety Function. The Manager, PV Analytics Center of Excellence contributes to the ongoing development, implementation, and successful execution of the scientific, operational, regulatory and custom reporting efforts in line with the overall WWPS needs. The Manager, PV Analytics Center of Excellence reports to the Associate Director, PV Analytics Center of Excellence, within Patient Safety organization. This person applies a combination of life sciences strategy, leadership, reporting/visualization and AI experience to drive successful servicing of information needs across WWPS. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following: Data Analytics and Reporting Build and continuously improve data analytics through supporting models that provide insights into efficiency, quality, stakeholder feedback, and key performance indicators to drive timely and informed decision making Maintain and develop reporting databases and analytics applications in environments such as MS Office Suite, Power BI, Cognos, SAP Business Objects, Spotfire and/or other BMS environments Leverage internal data systems and tools to efficiently maintain data and reporting processes to minimize manual data retrieving Champion the adoption and integration of AI-powered tools and platforms across the team, promoting a culture of innovation and continuous learning in alignment with BMS's enterprise AI strategy Contribute to qualitative and quantitative research projects through collaboration with data trends from cross-functional teams (Pharmacovigilance, Epidemiology, etc.) Utilize data analysis tools to aggregate and analyze data to make actionable recommendations and answer key business questions Run and maintain reports regarding activities, outcomes, and be prepared to deliver presentations to management team on a regular and ad-hoc basis Collect data for monthly reports and quarterly reviews regarding activities, outcomes, and trends of the Advisor team Analyze key stakeholder complaints, address rapidly, and discuss with applicable functional leads to collaborate and propose impactful and realistic solutions Maintain data integrity and traceability across the transformation lifecycle from Source to Target Support program and project team activities required to implement innovation initiatives, with a specific focus on AI-enabled process automation and intelligent analytics Contribute to the management and prioritization of process improvement and innovation initiatives Define and provide metric reporting and data analysis for PS initiatives including relevant insights to facilitate the decision-making process Assess and interpret the process impact of new PV tools and processes Skills/Knowledge Required: Life Sciences, Information, or similar background (Bachelor's, Master's) 5–7 years Drug Safety/Pharmacovigilance experience Advanced Power BI, Cognos, SAP Business Objects, Spotfire skills with 5–7 years of development experience Databases (Postgres, Oracle, MS Access, Databricks, Impala, SharePoint List, etc.) Programming languages (SQL, VBA, Python, etc.) Reporting platforms and services (Cognos, SAP Business Objects, etc.) Knowledge and application of commercial coding dictionaries (MedDRA, WHO Drug) Ability to organize/curate data and see the big picture from scattered pieces of information Knowledge of taxonomies, ontologies, and other knowledge management constructs Analytical and strategic thinking skills required Strong PowerPoint, Word, and Excel skills Knowledge of validation processes and associated documentation — including AI/ML model validation Excellent verbal, writing, presentation, and project management skills Strong strategic orientation with ability to translate into operational priorities and plans Ability to promote cooperation and commitment within a team to achieve goals and deliverables Ability to resolve complex problems and manage difficult stakeholder situations Ability to lead the development of critical path analyses and support scenario planning Promotes and practices effective pro-active decision-making, ensuring timely coordination and dissemination of information Demonstrated ability to work on multiple projects Strong willingness to collaborate with cross-functional partners Growth mindset with a passion for leveraging emerging AI technologies to solve real-world Drug Safety and PV challenges Flexible team member with positive attitude, friendly demeanor, ability to prioritize projects and balance competing priorities Confidentiality and integrity are required Skills/Knowledge Preferred: Familiarity with AI/ML concepts including supervised/unsupervised learning, natural language processing (NLP), large language models (LLMs), and Generative AI tools Demonstrated ability to evaluate and onboard AI/GenAI tools within enterprise environments, including prompt engineering and use case development Python libraries for AI/ML such as scikit-learn, pandas, or experience with LLM APIs (e.g., OpenAI, Azure OpenAI) We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway. How We Work Where you work matters – because collaboration, innovation and patient impact happen in many settings. Our roles are structured across four work models: site-essential, site-by-design, field-based and remote-by-design. The model assigned to this role is based on its core responsibilities. jobs.title: Security Engineer - Incident Response
jobs.description: Replit is the agentic software creation platform that enables anyone to build applications using natural language. With millions of users worldwide, Replit is democratizing software development by removing traditional barriers to application creation. ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for a Security Engineer with deep incident response experience to help defend Replit, a fast-moving, cloud-native AI vibe-coding platform. You'll be the person who takes charge when something goes wrong. You'll lead investigations from first signal to root cause, coordinate containment across Security, SRE, and Engineering, and keep stakeholders informed while the incident is moving fast. This isn't a pure responder role. We want a well-rounded security engineer who has run real incidents and wants to make the next one faster. You'll write the scripts, automations, and tooling that take manual work out of triage, evidence collection, and containment. You'll also turn lessons from each incident into better detections, playbooks, and platform hardening. RESPONSIBILITIES Incident Response - Serve as incident commander or technical lead for security incidents, from detection and triage through containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident review. - Coordinate response across Security, SRE, Engineering, Legal, and leadership. Drive decisions under pressure and keep a clear record of actions taken. - Communicate incident status, impact, and risk clearly to technical and executive audiences. - Participate in and help shape the security on-call rotation. Investigation & Forensics - Investigate suspicious activity across cloud infrastructure, containers, identity systems, and application layers using SIEM, Cloud Logging, telemetry, and host and container artifacts. - Determine scope, root cause, attacker behavior, and blast radius for confirmed incidents. - Quickly assess whether emerging threats (0-days, active exploitation campaigns, bug bounty findings, customer reports) apply to Replit, and whether we're already affected. IR Automation & Tooling - Build scripts, automations, and tools (Python, Go, Bash, or directly on Replit) that speed up response, such as automated enrichment, evidence collection, credential and session revocation, workload isolation, and alert triage. - Develop and maintain response playbooks and runbooks, and automate them where possible. - Integrate response workflows with SIEM, SOAR, ticketing, and chat tooling to cut time-to-contain. Detection & Continuous Improvement - Turn incident findings into new or improved detections, logging coverage, and visibility. - Lead blameless post-incident reviews and drive remediation items to completion. - Run tabletop exercises and simulations to test readiness and find gaps. REQUIRED SKILLS & EXPERIENCE - Proven experience leading or serving as technical lead on security incidents in a cloud or SaaS environment. - Strong hands-on investigation skills with SIEM, cloud audit logs, and log-based analysis. Comfortable working through large datasets under time pressure. - Proficiency writing production-quality scripts or tools in Python, Go, or Bash for investigation and automation. - Solid knowledge of cloud architecture and security, especially Google Cloud Platform (IAM, audit logging, GKE, networking). - Working knowledge of Kubernetes and containers, including how to investigate and contain compromised workloads. - Understanding of identity systems, SaaS architectures, and common cloud attack paths (credential theft, privilege escalation, supply chain, token abuse). - Familiarity with software engineering fundamentals, CI/CD pipelines, and package ecosystems, so you can work effectively with Engineering on code-level fixes. - Understanding of IR frameworks and lifecycle (for example NIST 800-61), plus the vulnerability lifecycle and exploitability analysis. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS - Experience building or operating SOAR or other response automation platforms. - Digital forensics experience with cloud, Linux hosts, or containers. - Experience with threat intelligence, threat hunting, or security research. - Experience with bug bounty programs or coordinated vulnerability disclosure. - Familiarity with detection-as-code practices and writing detection rules. - Experience in fast-paced, cloud-native, or AI/ML-driven environments. - Relevant certifications (such as GCIH, GCFA, GCFR), or equivalent hands-on experience. WHAT WE VALUE - Curiosity & initiative: Strong desire to understand attacker behaviors, emerging threats, and how they apply to real-world systems. - Speed & analytical rigor: Ability to quickly assess high-risk vulnerabilities with clear, evidence-based reasoning. - Collaboration: Comfort working across cross-functional teams spanning Security, SRE, Engineering, and Infrastructure. - Clear communication: Ability to explain findings, risks, and mitigation strategies to stakeholders at all levels. - Ownership mindset: Takes initiative to drive investigations, improvements, and remediations to completion. - Continuous learning: Passion for staying up to date on new vulnerabilities, exploit trends, and cloud-native security best practices. As a SOQ Specialist, your knowledge and skills will contribute towards the goals and objectives of the team. Your focus and ability to meet team targets will help in completing critical deliverables. Your innovative use of communication tools and techniques will facilitate explaining difficult issues and establishing consensus between teams. Key Accountabilities Resolution of Product Quality and Compliance Issues Deviation Management Investigates, together with appropriate local functions, deviations from Product Quality and Compliance requirements that occur within the responsibility of the PCO and agrees and tracks preventive/corrective actions. Local investigations may relate to product damage, artwork and labeling errors, counterfeits, temperature excursions during transport or issues with contract manufacturers or logistics service providers etc. Customer Complaints Handling Ensures that relevant customer complaints are dealt with effectively as the main responsibility. Notification to Management Informs PGS Quality Operations Management of significant deviations and complaints. Quality Management System Ensures timely implementation of all applicable Product Quality SOPs (issued by SOQ) within the PCO. Active involvement in Pfizer internal and external meetings from commercial perspective. Identifies personal areas of improvement. Maintains a good work-lifebalance. Ambitious companies and enduring institutions like Bridgewater, Lyft, Reddit, rely on Meter to keep their thousands of employees and locations online and productive. Our bet with Meter is simple: we will all use the internet more than we do today. We believe we have the definitive networking stack in place to enable business to do so as seamlessly and reliably as any modern utility. jobs.title: Staff + Software Security Engineer, Labs
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Frontier AI is on track to be among the most consequential and most adversarially-targeted technology in the world. The capability curve is steep, the adversaries who want these systems are extremely well-resourced, and the security bar this will eventually require is well beyond where the industry operates today. Incremental hardening alone is not going to close that gap, so we need breakthroughs and a group of people to go find them. Security Labs is that team. We run a portfolio of high-risk, high-expected-value security projects: the work that seems impractical until someone optimistic and stubborn enough actually tries it. Projects run on the order of weeks rather than quarters, and each one is either handed off to the Anthropic team that will own it in production or wound down with a writeup of what we learned. We expect a meaningful fraction of our bets not to land. This team is intentionally scrappy and ambitious. We're intentionally iterating fast on high-risk research bets and we expect a meaningful fraction not to land. If a 30% project success rate sounds uncomfortable, or uncharted and chaotic territory isn’t both frightening and exciting, this probably isn't the right fit. There are other places in Anthropic Security doing important work with more structure, less risk, and more certain paths to positive outcomes. The questions we're trying to answer include: Can our core research workflows survive extreme isolation? Can we replace trust with cryptographic guarantees? Can the models themselves become our most effective security control? What would it actually take to defend against a tier-1 state adversary, and how much of that can we build now? Who we're looking for. We're hiring generalists with rare depth. You're a strong software engineer as a baseline, and on top of that you've gone deep in at least one area most engineers don't get near: firmware or hardware security, applied cryptography, OS / kernel / hypervisor internals, formal methods, reverse engineering, or high-assurance and cross-domain systems. You've built things under your own direction, you're comfortable jumping layers when the problem demands it, and you'd rather take a swing at something that might not work than ship the safe incremental thing. You think the trajectory of AI matters a great deal, you're not comfortable with how the security side of it is going by default, and you'd rather be on the inside building the answer than watching from outside. Current Project Areas The portfolio changes as we learn. The kinds of bets currently in flight or queued: Standing up a prototype high-assurance research cluster: running real Anthropic training and research workloads under extreme isolation and physical security controls, and finding out exactly where productivity breaks and what we'd need to invent to get it back Provable inference: cryptographic verification (zero-knowledge proofs, attestation chains) that a given output came from a specific model running specific code, replacing "trust us" with math Build hypervisor-isolated microVM workload isolation across the fleet Compiling an ML kernel through a formally verified pipeline where every lowering step carries a machine-checked proof of equivalence, making compilation-layer sabotage mathematically detectable Regenerating clusters: automation that spins up a purpose-built cell, runs a workload, and tears the whole thing down on a TTL measured in hours, so attacker persistence has an expiry date Using Claude itself to drive security work end to end: threat modeling new compute platforms, rewriting critical services to zero external dependencies, running the test equipment that validates what hardware datasheets claim Part of your job is deciding what comes next. We hire people we trust to pick good bets, and project selection is owned by the engineers doing the work. Key responsibilities Own Security Labs projects end to end. You'll scope the bet, build the prototype, run it against real workloads, and bring it to either a hand-off or a documented exit Stand up novel security infrastructure fast (isolated clusters, attestation chains, hypervisor and runtime work, verification tooling) optimizing for what we learn rather than for permanence Find the receiving team early, bring them along while you build, and hand them something they actually want to own Work embedded with research and infrastructure teams (Pretraining, RL, Inference, Compute) to test whether their workflows survive what you're proposing, and document precisely where they don't Turn experimental results into short writeups that shape Anthropic's long-term security architecture, and into costed contingency plans we could execute on short notice Help pick the next round of bets and influence the industry to get better along the way Minimum qualifications Genuinely care about where AI is heading and want to work on the security problems that determine whether it goes well. This is the most important thing on this list Have real depth in at least one area most software engineers don't touch (e.g. firmware or hardware security, applied cryptography, OS / kernel / hypervisor internals, formal methods and verification, reverse engineering and exploit development, or high-assurance / cross-domain systems) Have built and shipped things under your own direction. Maybe you founded a company or research group, maintained an open-source project other people depend on, or shipped research that changed how people in your field work. We weight this far more than where you've worked or for how long Have a track record of choosing the problem yourself and seeing it through, rather than only executing a plan someone else handed you Are comfortable jumping between domains and layers of the stack when the problem calls for it, and have actually done so Have run prototypes or experiments where the goal was answering a hard question rather than shipping a permanent system, including ones that didn't pan out Write clearly enough to turn weeks of work into a couple of pages someone can act on Change your mind when the evidence says to, and are fine being the least-expert person in a room full of specialists Care about defense. Plenty of folks here come from offense and that background is valuable, but what you actually want to spend your time on now is making systems hold up Are a strong programmer (Python plus at least one of Rust, Go, or C/C++) and can stand up real infrastructure without that being the interesting part of your week Preferred qualifications Experience inside airgapped or high-side environments (classified networks, cross-domain solutions, ICS/SCADA, financial trading infrastructure) and the operational realities of working in them A background in offensive security, red teaming, or vulnerability research, with calibrated intuitions for which threats actually matter Familiarity with ML infrastructure (training pipelines, distributed schedulers, inference serving, accelerator hardware) sufficient for grounded conversations with researchers about what their workloads actually need A history of working in environments built around rapid iteration rather than rigid change control: startups, applied research groups, independent consulting, small security shops The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $485,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. <…

jobs.description: ABOUT RAMP Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. ABOUT THE ROLE Ramp is building a dedicated function to drive its partnerships across the AI ecosystem — labs, AI-native companies, and the investor community — and convert those into real technical and commercial outcomes. This is a newly created, high-visibility role that sits at the intersection of strategic business development, product partnership, and ecosystem relationship-building. Ramp is already embedded with key partners across the AI ecosystem, from working with leading labs on the latest models to serving as a design partner for emerging product capabilities. This role exists to deepen those relationships across every major lab and AI-native company, and turn them into something commercially meaningful. There is no playbook for this. This person will own and grow Ramp's most strategic relationships across the AI ecosystem, leading the technical side of those relationships end to end with partner product and engineering teams. The mandate spans product integrations, technical partnership strategy, deal-making, co-selling, and the creation of new revenue channels, pairing real product and engineering depth with commercial execution and ecosystem credibility. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Demonstrate technical depth to lead AI product and integration conversations end to end with partner engineering and product teams. - Own Ramp's relationships with emerging labs and AI-native companies at a true partnership level — not account management - Be embedded in the San Francisco AI community and know who is actually driving decisions at the labs, not just what the org chart says - Convert ecosystem relationships into commercial outcomes — referrals, integrations, co-selling, and new revenue channels - Do both the business development and product/integration work, combining deal-making with genuine technical engagement - Stay ahead of how leading AI companies are commercializing and going to market, and help Ramp move with them — and ahead of them - Represent Ramp externally across the San Francisco AI community: founders, investors, lab leaders, and operators WHAT YOU'LL NEED - Deep, trusted relationships at leading AI companies with the people who make decisions and influence direction — not just formal contacts - Commercial outcomes tied to those relationships, including initiatives with measurable revenue potential and smarter product integrations on both sides - Ramp is known and respected across the San Francisco AI community as a must-know fintech partner - Ramp keeps pace with — and ideally stays ahead of — how quickly the labs are changing, evolving their go-to-market strategies, and commercializing - A repeatable business development and product motion built for the AI ecosystem, not a series of one-off partnerships - An ever-evolving AI partnership strategy that includes sourcing, negotiating, contracting, executing, and growing relationships with leading AI companies Over the course of a year, success means launching public products, integrations, go-to-market initiatives, and distribution channels with labs and applied AI companies. Near-term objectives could include inclusion in model-launch announcements and joint product-integration launches. Longer-term goals will incorporate adoption of integrations and revenue targets as distribution partnerships are executed. Every day will look different, but the work will include meeting with cross-functional stakeholders internally and externally, keeping a pulse on applied AI and the labs, negotiating active contracts, refining and executing Ramp's AI partnership strategy, and helping Ramp get closer to the teams that matter at the top AI companies. NICE TO HAVES - The ideal candidate combines two qualities that are hard to find in one person: ECOSYSTEM CONNECTOR - Deep personal relationships in the San Francisco AI community — founders, lab leaders, and investors — at a level where people pick up the phone - Experience working inside or alongside leading AI partners in a way that provides genuine credibility, not just familiarity - Known and trusted by the venture capital and investor community in AI COMMERCIAL OPERATOR - Has built partnerships from zero at a high-growth company and been accountable for commercial outcomes - Can do the product and business development work simultaneously — technically fluent enough to engage on integrations and commercially sharp enough to close deals - Has a builder mindset and can design scalable programs, not just one-off relationships KEY CRITERIA - Strategic business development — can identify and close partnerships that drive real commercial outcomes - Technical aptitude — enough depth to hold credible conversations with AI lab and product teams - Systems thinking — builds scalable programs, not just one-off deals - Access — personal relationships at the decision-maker level inside labs, AI-native companies, and the investor community WHY THIS ROLE IS EXCITING - Ramp's AI partners are among the most influential partners any technology company can have right now. jobs.title: Strategy and Operations, OpenAI for Government
jobs.description: ABOUT THE TEAM The OpenAI for Government team is a dynamic, mission-driven group leveraging frontier AI to transform how governments achieve their missions. Our team works to empower public servants with secure, compliant AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT Enterprise in custom configurations) and mission-aligned deployments that meet government technical requirements with strong reliability and safety. As part of the OpenAI for Government team you will work across governments and public institutions, helping to accelerate adoption through hands-on support, tailored training, and early insights—so civil servants can spend less time on red tape and more on meaningful work. If you're passionate about responsibly deploying frontier AI to uplift public institutions and transform how the government serves the American people, we want you on our team. ABOUT THE ROLE We are looking for an experienced strategy and business operations professional to help OpenAI for Government decide where to grow and how to build the capabilities needed to serve government customers. You will shepherd ambiguous, complex work from problem definition through execution. The majority of the role will focus on business strategy and operations, from market and revenue planning to workforce, financial, and secure facility initiatives. You should be skilled at both developing a compelling recommendation and doing the detailed work to make it happen. This role has four key buckets of responsibilities: - First, you will support the growth and maturation of a business operations and revenue strategy function within the OpenAI for Government. You will help OpenAI for Government four vertical leaders develop annual business strategies that define target customers, priority projects, partners, and support needed from other matrixed teams including Technical Success, Engineering, Capture and Proposal, Global Affairs, and Product Policy. - You will build and maintain the intelligence picture for our key territories: mission priorities, budget lines and program timelines, incumbents and competitive positions, and the people who actually shape awards. - You will act as a thought partner to the business verticals by participating in weekly team discussions to understand the business, test assumptions, and identify risks. You will run quarterly reviews to track progress, reassess goals, and adjust priorities. - Second, you will partner with OpenAI’s industrial security team to forecast secure-space needs, plan SCIF buildouts, coordinate personnel access nominations, and track contract-specific security requirements and restrictions. - Third, you will support OpenAI’s Government Innovation Network, OpenAI for Government’s advisory board, throughout the entire lifecycle of the program, including advisor outreach and selection, independent-contractor agreements (1099s), conflict reviews, payment, and high-touch onboarding. - In partnership with OpenAI for Government’s leadership team, you will help design and run regular advisor meetings, quarterly strategy sessions, and targeted convenings, with clear agendas, materials, and decisions. You will execute follow-through, and ensure advisor insights are integrated into OpenAI for Government’s strategy. - Finally, you will own and drive special projects that do not yet have a clear home. You will define the problem, develop options, build consensus, and lead early execution. YOU’LL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU: - Have experience in strategy consulting, business operations, a growing technology company, or comparable work combining analytical problem-solving with ownership of execution. - Can build financial models, size markets, assess competitive positions, and translate incomplete data into recommendations with clear assumptions and tradeoffs. Are comfortable interpreting government budgets and using market intelligence sources such as Janes to inform long-term investment decisions. - Create compelling executive presentations and write concise memos that connect the numbers, strategic choices, and recommended actions. - Can define an unfamiliar problem before solving it, learn new technologies and markets quickly, and make progress without a fully formed brief. - Enjoy a broad remit and move comfortably between strategic analysis, business operations, and detailed project delivery. - Build trust with executives, government stakeholders, advisors, and technical specialists, and influence across functions without formal authority. - Bring strong judgment and discretion to sensitive relationships, personnel matters, compensation, and security-related work. - Are comfortable managing budgets, vendors, contractors, and competing deadlines, and take responsibility for carrying work through to completion. - Are curious about government missions, procurement, policy, and funding. Direct public-sector, defense, or national-security experience is valuable, alongside strong business and analytical skills. - Are willing to travel periodically for advisor convenings, agency or customer engagements, and operational projects. - Care deeply about the mission and want to help build a durable government business grounded in the responsible deployment of frontier AI. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. jobs.description: POSITION SUMMARY: The Organ Health Patient Coordinator (PC) is the primary point of contact and dedicated advocate for patients undergoing organ health genetic testing. This role sits at the heart of Natera's mission — ensuring that every patient is supported, informed, and guided with care through each step of their testing journey. This position will be focused on growing the relationship between Natera and its patients to ensure timely management of testing. Organ Health patients may require a single test or ongoing, long-term monitoring — in either case, the relationships PCs build are essential, whether that means earning the trust of a new patient to complete their first draw or maintaining continuity with patients throughout a recurring testing journey. A natural drive to overcome objections and convert hesitant patients into confident ones is key to growing the business and ensuring no patient is left behind. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: Serve as the patient's dedicated advocate and single point of contact for all things related to their Organ Health testing experience. Assess the needs of patients with a focus on customer support, coordination of logistics, and problem solving. Set accurate expectations around sample collection scheduling, turnaround time, billing, and next steps to ensure patients feel informed and confident. Respond to patient-generated marketing leads and conduct outbound outreach for applicable patient identification and monitoring programs. Appropriately triage and escalate complex issues to cross-functional partners including the MP Team, Organ Health Specialists (OHS/Sales), Territory Managers, Customer Experience, and Billing Teams. Participate in rotating weekend on-call coverage to ensure urgent patient needs are addressed in a timely manner. Maintain and support a service-oriented relationship with patients Ensure all data and analysis requests from different parts of the organization are addressed in a timely manner. Identify, nurture and grow patient relationships in order to influence and schedule ongoing testing. Performs other duties as assigned. This role works with PHI on a regular basis both in paper and electronic form and has access to various technologies to access PHI (paper and electronic) in order to perform the job. Adhere strictly to HIPAA regulations, including verifying patient identity on every interaction conducted. Employees must complete training relating to HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure Compliance training and security training as soon as possible but not later than the first 30 days of hire. Must maintain a current status on Natera training requirements. QUALIFICATIONS: Minimum of 2 years of Call Center experience in an inbound and outbound capacity, patient services, or healthcare customer support role. Minimum of 2 years of sales experience Background in medical or biological sciences preferred KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES: Genuine empathy and compassion; Strong active listening and rapport-building skills with the ability to handle emotionally complex conversations professionally. Ability to think strategically as well as execute tactically Emphasis on competitive analysis and team first attitude. cold_email.subject: Interest in Patient Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Patient Coordinator opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.description: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. Our goal is to democratize data, support Cloudflare’s critical business needs, provide reporting and analytics via self-service data applications to fuel existing and new business critical initiatives. jobs.description: ABOUT RAMP Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. ABOUT THE ROLE Buying something for a business should not require finance teams to piece together requests, purchase orders, receipts, and invoices across disconnected systems. Ramp is building a procurement experience that helps employees get what they need, gives finance teams control over commitments, and helps businesses pay for what they actually received. As a Product Manager for Ramp’s Procurement offering, you will own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for Ramp’s core procurement capabilities, including sourcing, requisition, approval workflows, renewals, purchase orders, receiving, two- and three-way matching, and inventory management. You will work with Engineering, Design, and Data to turn complex purchasing and accounting requirements into products that are easy to start using and reliable as customers grow. AI creates an opportunity to rethink this work: build agentic buying experiences for employees, automate work for approvers and stakeholders, and businesses make better purchasing decisions. You will decide where automation can take work off a customer’s plate, where a direct workflow is faster, and where a person needs to review or approve an action. Success means customers get value quickly, adopt the product in their everyday work, and spend less time chasing information and correcting errors. This role requires working in person at our NYC or SF office at least two days per week. Please note that this role requires in-person presence at our NYC or SF office at least 2 days/week. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Own the strategy and roadmap for Ramp’s Procurement pod. Make clear choices about which customer problems to solve, how the capabilities fit together, and what to build next. - Build connected workflows across sourcing, requisition, approvals, renewals, purchase orders, receiving, invoice matching, and inventory management. Partner with Bill Pay, Accounting, and platform teams so purchasing records and decisions carry through to payment and customers’ ERP systems. - Spend time with finance teams, procurement leaders, purchasing operators, and employees. Turn observed friction into simpler experiences for first-time customers and powerful workflows for complex organizations. - Build AI-powered experiences that complete useful work, such as finding new vendors, managing a renewal, drafting a request from a contract, or helping resolve a receipt and invoice discrepancy. Prototype with customers and decide what should be automated, suggested, or handled through direct user controls. - Make automation dependable. Partner with Engineering and Data to define quality measures, test realistic customer scenarios, learn from corrections, and provide clear explanations, approval boundaries, audit trails, and recovery when something goes wrong. - Own outcomes beyond launch. Define and improve activation, repeat usage, time to complete purchasing work, and the accuracy of matching and exception resolution. Use data and customer research to choose the next iteration. - Lead execution with engineers and designers, make scope and sequencing tradeoffs, and align partner teams on dependencies. Work with Sales, Implementation, and Customer Experience to turn customer commitments into repeatable product capabilities and support successful adoption. WHAT YOU NEED - At least three years of product management or equivalent product-building experience, with evidence of owning a product area from customer discovery through launch and measurable adoption. - Strong product judgment and systems thinking. You can simplify complex workflows while preserving the controls and flexibility customers need. - Hands-on AI fluency, demonstrated through products, prototypes, or meaningful projects. You can reason about model quality, latency, cost, and user control, and choose where AI improves the experience. - Technical and analytical fluency, developed through a technical or analytical degree or equivalent practical experience. You can work with engineers on data models and integrations, use data to investigate problems, and build prototypes to test ideas. - Deep customer curiosity and strong design judgment. You can learn unfamiliar purchasing and finance workflows, distinguish recurring needs from one-off requests, and make the product easier to use. - A track record of leading cross-functional teams, setting priorities, making difficult tradeoffs, and delivering outcomes through others. - Clear written and verbal communication. You can explain a product direction, a complex workflow, and the reasoning behind a decision to technical and non-technical audiences. NICE-TO-HAVES - Experience with procurement, purchasing, inventory management, accounts payable, or accounting software, including purchase orders, receiving, matching, and exception handling. - Experience shipping AI-powered products used in production, including document understanding, agent workflows, and evaluation systems. - Experience with ERP integrations, multi-entity businesses, or enterprise approval and permission models. - Experience building products where accuracy and trust matter, with meaningful auditability, user controls, and recovery paths. - Experience at a high-growth startup, taking new products from initial concept to sustained use or scaling an existing product. cold_email.subject: Interest in Information Security Analyst — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Information Security Analyst opportunity with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: AV Engineer, Platform & Automation
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the Role As an AV Engineer focused on Platform & Automation, you'll build and own the software layer of Anthropic's collaboration systems — the tools, integrations, and engineering practices that let a small AV team support a fast-growing global office portfolio. Our rooms, event spaces, and broadcast systems are increasingly managed through APIs and code: device management platforms, DSP and control systems, conferencing administration, ticketing, and paging. Your job is to turn that surface into reliable, team-owned tooling, and to bring software engineering discipline to how we build and maintain it. You can expect a lot of your time writing, shipping, and operating code — fleet health monitoring, automated room testing and ticketing, integrations between our AV platforms and IT systems, and the internal tools that AV Engineering, AV Operations, and Events rely on every day. You'll also help own the administration of the software platforms we already run, and set the standards for how the team version-controls, reviews, tests, releases, and maintains everything from DSP designs to firmware to internal services. Responsibilities Design, build, and ship internal tools and integrations that monitor, test, and manage AV and collaboration systems across every office Develop fleet health monitoring and automated room testing that catch failures before users report them and open actionable tickets automatically Build integrations across device and platform APIs — Q-SYS (including plugins and Lua control scripts), Logitech Sync, Google Meet hardware, digital signage; and IT systems such as Jira, Slack, PagerDuty, and Google Workspace Automate repetitive operational work: provisioning, configuration baselines, drift detection, certificate renewal, and asset data — with code others can read, test, and maintain Own administration and lifecycle of the software platforms behind the AV estate, including firmware and software release management with staged rollouts and rollback plans Operate internal tools as production services, with monitoring, alerting, service metrics, and runbooks, on team-owned repositories and service identities so nothing depends on one person Establish the team's engineering practices: source control, code review, testing, CI/CD, and release — and bring AV configuration under version control, with standards set for integrator deliverables and acceptance verified before changes land Enable AV Engineers, Operations Specialists, and Production staff to contribute safely through templates, guardrails, and review paths built for non-developers Partner with Security, IT Engineering, and Network on least-privilege API access, secrets management, and integration with enterprise standards Gather requirements from AV Operations, Events, and AV Engineering, prioritize the tooling roadmap by operational impact, and decide where to build, buy, or push a vendor to close a gap You May Be a Good Fit If You: Have 10+ years of experience across AV, collaboration, or IT systems engineering, including 4+ years writing, shipping, and maintaining production code that other people depend on Are fluent in at least one general-purpose language: Python, Lua, Go, TypeScript, or similar — and comfortable with shell scripting Practice engineering fundamentals by default: Git-based workflows, code review, automated testing, CI/CD, logging, and observability Understand how AV and collaboration systems work: DSP and control, conferencing platforms, room devices, signal flow, AV-over-IP — well enough to build reliable tools on top of them Have built integrations against REST APIs, webhooks, and vendor SDKs, and know how to handle auth, rate limits, pagination, retries, and partial failure Have owned a tool or service in production over time, not just written it, including fixing it when it broke and handing it off cleanly Have defined engineering practices for a team, especially one where most contributors aren't developers Turn operational pain into well-scoped tooling, and can say no to work that shouldn't be built Thrive in a fast-moving environment where standards are being written rather than inherited Strong Candidates May Also Have Experience With: Q-SYS Lua scripting and plugin development Logitech Sync and CollabOS, and Google Meet hardware administration through the Google Admin console and Admin SDK Google Workspace APIs, GCP (Cloud Run, Cloud Scheduler, Pub/Sub, Secret Manager), and Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code Jira, Slack, and PagerDuty APIs and automation Crestron, Extron, or other control system programming Dante, AES67, NDI, and network fundamentals for AV-over-IP, including multicast, VLANs, and QoS Building with LLMs — agentic automation, LLM-assisted internal tools, or MCP integrations Monitoring and alerting stacks such as Prometheus and Grafana, and containerized deployment Q-SYS Level 2, CTS, or equivalent demonstrated capability Role Specific Location Policy: This role will be based in our San Francisco or New York City office This role is expected to be in office 50% of the time Up to 4 weeks of domestic and international travel annually for platform rollouts, new-office readiness, and on-site testing Business-hours escalation coverage for the tools and platforms this role owns Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be received on a rolling basis. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $285,000 — $325,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.
